rice.name: Rice
rice.soil: Rice grows well in fertile clayey or loamy soil with good water-holding capacity.
rice.water: Rice generally needs sufficient water, especially during important growth stages. Avoid unnecessary waterlogging when it is not required.
tips: Use healthy and good-quality seeds.
Maintain proper spacing between plants.
Monitor the field regularly for weeds and pests.
Use fertilizers according to soil requirements.

tomato.name: Tomato
tomato.soil: Tomato grows well in fertile, well-drained soil rich in organic matter.
tomato.water: Provide regular and consistent watering. Avoid both prolonged dryness and excessive watering.
tips: Provide adequate sunlight.
Maintain proper spacing for good air circulation.
Monitor leaves and fruits regularly for pests and diseases.
Use balanced nutrients based on soil conditions.

cotton.name: Cotton
cotton.soil: Cotton grows well in deep, fertile and well-drained soils.
cotton.water: Cotton needs adequate moisture during important growth stages, but excessive water should be avoided.
tips: Use suitable varieties for the local climate.
Monitor regularly for insect pests.
Keep the field free from excessive weeds.
Follow recommended fertilizer practices.

groundnut.name: Groundnut
groundnut.soil: Groundnut prefers loose, well-drained sandy loam or loamy soil.
groundnut.water: Provide adequate moisture during germination, flowering and pod development.
tips: Use good-quality seeds.
Avoid waterlogging.
Control weeds during early crop growth.
Monitor the crop for leaf diseases and insect pests.

chilli.name: Chilli
chilli.soil: Chilli grows well in fertile and well-drained loamy soil.
chilli.water: Water regularly according to soil moisture and weather conditions. Avoid excessive watering.
tips: Use healthy seedlings.
Maintain proper spacing.
Monitor plants for sucking pests.
Remove severely affected plant parts when appropriate.

soil_health: Test soil before making major fertilizer decisions.
Adding suitable organic matter can improve soil structure and fertility.
pest_management: Inspect crops regularly for early signs of pests.
Prefer appropriate and recommended control methods based on the identified pest.
Do not use pesticides without following the product label and local agricultural guidance.
water_management: Irrigate according to crop stage, soil condition and weather.
Use efficient irrigation methods where practical.
weather: Check local weather conditions before irrigation or spraying.
Heavy rain can increase the risk of waterlogging and some crop diseases.
Strong winds and extreme temperatures can affect crop growth.
